summary: A first-person narrator from a near-future Xnet-centered story recounts a hungover Saturday in San Francisco's Mission district after a night of flirting with Ange until 4AM. Walking out, he sees fresh graffiti, including the words DON'T TRUST ANYONE OVER 25 painted on an auto-yard fence, and learns through anonymous Xnet blogs that a concert in the park with that name has grown into a movement. He reflects on feeling alone, avoiding calls to Van, Jolu and Darryl, and plans to revisit an anarchist bookstore on Monday.
one_line: A narrator in the Mission district learns from Xnet blogs that a park concert called Don't Trust Anyone Over 25 has become a youth movement.
key_facts: The narrator's school route passed a poster of Emma Goldman with the caption "If I can't dance, I don't want to be a part of your revolution."
The narrator had been spending his energies on using the Xnet to organize dedicated fighters to jam the DHS.
The narrator was a zombie the next day because he and Ange had chatted and flirted until 4AM.
The day in question was a Saturday, so the narrator could sleep in.
The narrator liked Mission graffiti, which often came in huge murals or sarcastic art-student stencils.
Some surveillance cameras in the Mission had been spray-painted over.
Painted in ten-foot-high letters on the side of an auto-yard's fence were the words DON'T TRUST ANYONE OVER 25.
The narrator could not call Van, who was not talking to him, and did not feel ready to talk to Jolu.
Anonymous Xnet blogs, called anonablogs, were untraceable to any author unless the author put her name on it.
Plans for a concert in the park had existed for weeks and had hopped from blog to blog.
The concert was called Don't Trust Anyone Over 25.
The narrator concluded that the slogan explained where Ange got it from.
On Monday morning, the narrator decided he wanted to check out the anarchist bookstore again.
